content: {"summary":"On 24 Mar 2026 inventory‑service pods could not resolve their DB hostname while datastore VMs could because the two internal DNS servers were temporarily out of sync. Pods use the cluster CoreDNS forwarder which picks one of the two authoritative servers at random, so some queries hit the server that lacked the record. VMs resolve via /etc/resolv.conf ordering, typically using the first server which still had the correct record, so they succeeded.","likely_cause":"A partial rollout of the prod.internal zone left the inventory‑db‑01 record missing on one of the internal‑dns servers, causing random pod queries to fail while VM queries succeeded via the other server.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"Pods resolve via cluster CoreDNS which forwards queries randomly to the two internal DNS servers","evidence_ids":["RB-020#3"],"quote":"The `forward` plugin picks an upstream at random for each query it sends."},{"text":"VMs resolve using the first DNS server listed in /etc/resolv.conf and only fall back if it fails","evidence_ids":["RB-020#2"],"quote":"VMs list both servers in `/etc/resolv.conf`, internal-dns-01 first."},{"text":"During a rollout the two authoritative DNS servers can temporarily differ, causing a missing record on one server","evidence_ids":["RB-020#2","RB-020#10"],"quote":"The rollout tool updates them one after the other, so for a short time during a rollout the two can differ."}],"next_checks":["Run `dig @10.0.0.53 inventory-db-01.prod.internal +norecurse` and `dig @10.0.0.54 …` to see which server returns NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL","Compare SOA serial numbers on both internal‑dns servers with `dig @10.0.0.53 prod.internal SOA +short` etc.","Inspect the zone file on each server for the `inventory-db-01` record (`grep` the file paths)","Check the rollout logs to see if a zone update was in progress on 24 Mar 2026","Review CoreDNS pod logs for cache hits/misses during the incident period"]}
